contract_why: Scope audit of the whole paper directory. The flags sit only on summary surfaces: the abstract (main.tex, B.1), the introduction's result paragraphs, its literature paragraph and its 1.1 trust base with Table 1 (B.2), the concluding remarks with their scope and open questions (08-conclusions.tex, B.9; that section has no separate discussion, so B.8 is not declared), the captions, and the numbered section maps in 03, 05 and 07 that restate results by \ref. Each claim was restated from its cited statement in 03-07 before being compared with the summary. I used the paper's own role for each file and ignored the template's section numbers.
strengths: The summaries are mostly careful about the frontier. The conclusions name the Student-t hypothesis and the cited Bessel and moment clauses. Section 1.1 lists the seven unformalized items and prints the axiom output of the headline declaration. Remarks cin-propagation, rational-converse and dimension-filtration mark what is expected and not proved.
floor: linkage check / linkage axioms: noted, not run; a scope audit does not work the integrity floor

anchor: a kernel is bounded at the origin exactly when its profile starts above one
claim: Corollary origin-boundedness assumes Gaussian coefficient 0 and a finite positive k(0+). Any member with a>0 is bounded whatever k(0+) is, and the case k(0+)=infinity (the stable members, Thorin members with unbounded U) is explicitly not claimed. The abstract's 'exactly when' covers both.
probe: Restate the corollary's two hypotheses (no Gaussian part, finite k(0+)) in the sentence, or check whether the a>0 and k(0+)=infinity cases are covered anywhere.

anchor: An admissible kernel is bounded at the origin exactly when its profile starts above $1$
claim: Quantifies over every admissible kernel. Corollary origin-boundedness holds only with a=0 and k(0+) finite; with a Gaussian part the kernel is bounded for every profile, which makes the 'exactly when' false.
probe: Carry the corollary's quantifier ('without Gaussian part, with k(0+) finite') into the sentence.

anchor: bounded at the origin exactly when the value of its profile there exceeds $1$
claim: 'The kernel of a member' drops the corollary's standing hypotheses a=0 and 0<k(0+)<infinity. Open question 5 reuses the threshold as if it were unconditional.
probe: Restate the hypotheses of cor:origin-boundedness here, then reread open question 5 against them.

anchor: decided by one number, the value $k(0{+})$ of the profile there
claim: The section map says what 'an admissible kernel' does at the origin is decided by k(0+). Proposition cin-origin-singularity is stated only for Gaussian coefficient 0, and the prose after it says nothing is claimed at k(0+)=infinity.
probe: Add 'with no Gaussian part' (and finite k(0+) for the trichotomy) to the map item, as the proposition has it.

anchor: characterized as the unique member with every moment finite, exponential tails and an exact implementation by first-order recursive filters
claim: The paper's own Proposition rational-increments(1) and Remark recursive-gaussians give other families with the same three properties: finite multi-range Matérn mixtures with integer weights have exponential-tailed profiles and are realized exactly by first-order forward-backward lag sections. Also, Proposition matern-cascade realizes only integer gamma, so the non-integer Matérn members lack the property the abstract attributes to 'the Matérn family'.
probe: Check what cor:matern-realization's uniqueness step actually uses (identical sections with a single pole pair, as in thm:matern(4)), state that restriction and integer gamma where the claim is made, and reconcile it with prop:rational-increments(1).

anchor: unique admissible family with every moment finite, exponential tails and an exact recursive implementation
claim: 'Exact recursive implementation' is wider than the corollary's own 'first-order forward-backward sections'. Even that is contradicted by prop:rational-increments(1), whose multi-range Matérn mixtures are exactly recursive with finite moments and exponential tails. The realization exists for integer gamma only. The same claim returns in the literature paragraph as 'the characterization of the Matérn family by exact implementability'.
probe: Restate cor:matern-realization's actual hypothesis (single pole pair, integer gamma), check its uniqueness proof against prop:rational-increments(1), and align this sentence and the literature paragraph with it.

anchor: is the unique admissible family with every moment finite, exponential tails and an exact recursive implementation
claim: The section map calls this the headline. Its uniqueness is contradicted two sections later by prop:rational-increments(1), where finite integer-weight Matérn mixtures have rational stages realized by the same lag sections. The corollary it paraphrases also omits integer gamma, which its realization half (prop:matern-cascade) needs.
probe: Compare the corollary's proof step 'a first-order forward-backward section has transfer function (1+theta^2 s^2 omega^2)/(1+theta^2 t^2 omega^2)' with rational-increments(1), where the sections have different theta_i; decide which restriction the uniqueness really carries.

anchor: the unique member with every moment finite, exponential tails and an exact recursive implementation
claim: The same uniqueness claim, cited to thm:matern and cor:matern-realization. Theorem matern characterizes by a single pole pair at integer gamma, not by exact recursive implementation, and prop:rational-increments(1) supplies other exactly recursive members with finite moments and exponential tails.
probe: Restate which of the two numbered results is being summarized, and check its quantifiers (single pole pair, integer gamma).

anchor: The \Matern{} family is characterized as the unique member
claim: The characterization the abstract states is cor:matern-realization. Section 1.1 lists it as not formalized, since it rests on the implementation section, and its proof also reads the cited closed form (prop:matern-density). The machine-checked headline is thm:matern. The abstract's closing 'Most of the results are machine-checked' leaves a reader to assume this one is.
probe: Check whether the abstract should summarize thm:matern (checked) or say at the point of claim that the implementability characterization is proved on paper.

anchor: all three families lie in one subcone, the profiles that are mixtures of exponentials
claim: The Student-t family's membership of the Thorin subclass is prop:student-t(3). That clause is conditional on the inverse-gamma law being a generalized gamma convolution (Halgreen, rem:student-ggc), and the conclusions say so. Here it is stated flatly.
probe: Mark the Student-t membership as conditional where the three families are grouped, as rem:cone-shape and the conclusions do.

anchor: a subcone that contains all three families
claim: The section map places all three families in the Thorin subcone unconditionally. prop:student-t(3) gives the Student-t case only under the GGC hypothesis of rem:student-ggc, and the text after prop:thorin-subclass itself says 'under the hypothesis stated there'.
probe: Carry the hypothesis of prop:student-t(3) into the map item.

anchor: it contains the Gaussian ray and all three named families
claim: The caption puts the Student-t family inside the image of the bridge. Lemma student-subordinated proves that only under the hypothesis that the inverse-gamma law is the delay law of a causally admissible exponent (rem:student-ggc). Lemma subordinated-members covers only the Gaussian ray, the Matérn family and the stable family.
probe: Mark the Student-t membership in the caption as conditional, or draw the Student-t ray differently.

anchor: the Student-t and stable families among them, are approximated from inside the class by families with such stages
claim: Proposition thorin-machine asserts weak convergence for positive-weight quadratures, and separately that rounding the weights to even integers keeps admissibility and makes the stages rational. It never asserts that the rounded (rational-stage) families still converge, which is what 'approximated by families with such stages' needs. It also realizes a Gaussian part 'separately', not by lag sections, and the Student-t member of the Thorin class is conditional (prop:student-t(3)).
probe: Check whether convergence survives the rounding to even integers (rounding a small weight to 0 or 2 is not a small change), and state in the summary only what prop:thorin-machine asserts.

anchor: is approximated from inside the class by families with rational stages
claim: The section map joins two things the proposition keeps apart. Convergence is stated for arbitrary positive quadratures, rational stages only after rounding to even integers, and no convergence is claimed for the rounded family. The prose before the statement ('both steps stay inside the admissible class and ... the kernels converge') repeats the joined reading.
probe: Restate prop:thorin-machine's two clauses separately, and check whether a convergence statement for even-integer weights is needed and provable.

anchor: Every member of the Thorin subclass is approximated from inside the class by families with such stages
claim: 'Every member of the Thorin subclass' includes members with a>0, whose Gaussian part prop:thorin-machine realizes 'separately' and not by first-order forward-backward stages. And the rational-stage (even-integer) approximants are not asserted to converge.
probe: Restrict to a=0, and check what the proposition asserts about the rounded family's convergence.

anchor: one explicit family shows that the chain is strict at its bottom
claim: Lemma filtration-strictness(2) asserts only that certain polar profiles are or are not nonincreasing. The conclusion A_1 != A_2 != A_3 is drawn in rem:dimension-filtration and needs two more steps: the cited polar criterion (A7), and the identification of the isotropic law's polar profile for a delay datum that is not causally admissible, which prop:dimension-filtration(2) proves only for causally admissible data. The lemma itself is typed and not machine-checked.
probe: Check whether the step from 'polar profile not nonincreasing' to 'F not in A_d' is stated anywhere as a numbered result; if not, say at this sentence that the strictness is read through the remark and the cited polar criterion.

anchor: the chain is strict at its bottom
claim: This cites prop:dimension-filtration and lem:filtration-strictness for strictness, but neither states it. The lemma states polar-profile monotonicity, and the passage to A_d membership is in rem:dimension-filtration, through the cited polar criterion.
probe: Name the remark and the cited criterion beside the lemma, or add the missing step as a numbered statement.

anchor: It misses every member whose profile is a lattice step
claim: Proposition bridge-strictness(3) gives a stationary point, and so non-subordination, only when a=0 and the Choquet measure is lattice-carried. A member with a>0 and a lattice-step profile has no stationary point, and nothing in the paper shows it is outside S.
probe: Restate '(with no Gaussian part)' from clause (3), or check whether the a>0 case is proved anywhere.

anchor: and every member whose profile is a lattice step, have no causal ancestor
claim: The section's motivation paragraph drops the a=0 that prop:bridge-strictness(3) needs for the stationary-point argument.
probe: Carry 'with no Gaussian part' from clause (3) into the sentence.

anchor: Symmetric self-decomposable laws with a lattice-step profile are therefore members
claim: The 'therefore' restates clause (3) of prop:bridge-strictness without its a=0. The criterion just discussed is a zero of the symbol B, which a Gaussian term 2a omega^2 > 0 removes.
probe: Restate the a=0 condition of clause (3) here.

anchor: the lattice-step members sit outside all of them at once
claim: This previews prop:dimension-filtration(3). The proof of (3) gets its stationary point from prop:bridge-strictness(3), which requires a=0, so 'the lattice-step members' holds only for the pure-jump ones.
probe: Check the a=0 condition through the chain of citations and restate it in the preview.

anchor: the lattice-step members of the line's theory lie outside $\mathcal{A}_\infty$
claim: The statement's own summary line and its clause (3) ('no admissible F not identically 0 whose profile is a step function with its jumps on a lattice') drop a=0. The proof of (3) invokes prop:bridge-strictness(3), which gives a stationary point only when a=0.
probe: Compare clause (3) with the hypothesis of the clause its proof cites; the fix is at the blueprint node.

anchor: which shows that a hard cutoff in the profile leaves echoes in the kernel at the multiples of $\tau$
claim: Lemma cin-delay-equation states only the delay equation. The echoes at multiples of tau are Remark cin-propagation, which says the induction is not carried out and that no result depends on it. The introduction says the lemma 'shows' it.
probe: Mark the echo structure as the remark's unproved description at the point of claim, or state and prove the propagation.

anchor: echoes the singularity at $\pm\tau$, $\pm2\tau$, one order of smoothness gained at each step
claim: The Figure cin-rays caption attributes the echoes to the delay equation of the lemma as a fact. Remark cin-propagation, which it cites, says the induction is not carried out and the description is not a claim.
probe: Mark in the caption that the echo description is the remark's, not proved; the dotted lines are then an illustration of an expectation.

anchor: whatever it does at the origin is echoed at $\pm\tau$
claim: The section map reads the echo structure off Lemma cin-delay-equation as settled. Remark cin-propagation, later in the section, says it is not proved.
probe: Mark the status here as the remark does.

anchor: a stage is a pair of first-order recursive filters
claim: Proposition matern-cascade realizes a stage for integer gamma as gamma causal plus gamma anticausal first-order sections, 2*gamma filters. 'A pair' is the gamma=1 case only.
probe: Count the sections in prop:matern-cascade and match the sentence to that count.

anchor: the theory says which of those filters are themselves scale spaces
claim: Remark recursive-gaussians gives only two partial answers. Real poles with P=1 are admissible. For complex poles it gives an infinite-divisibility test, but admissibility needs self-decomposability, which is stronger. Nothing settles which filters are scale spaces, and the remark is not a proved statement. The source comment still flags the literature anchor as unacquired.
probe: Restate what rem:recursive-gaussians actually establishes (a sufficient condition and a necessary one) and check whether 'says which' is supported.

anchor: It also says which of the recursive filters used to approximate the Gaussian are themselves scale spaces
claim: The map item credits prop:matern-cascade and rem:recursive-gaussians with a classification. The remark gives a sufficient condition (real poles) and an infinite-divisibility test that falls short of admissibility (self-decomposability) for complex poles. The paragraph after the map repeats the claim.
probe: Check the complex-pole case against self-decomposability rather than infinite divisibility, and narrow the summary to what the remark proves.

anchor: Every member's scale space solves an equation
claim: Proposition scale-evolution is proved for signals in the Schwartz class (def:signal-class), and Section 6 says that enlarging the class is open. The introduction, the abstract and the conclusions state the evolution for every member with no signal class, in a paper whose stated model is L^1.
probe: Name the signal class where the evolution equation is summarized.

anchor: everything, on Lean's logical foundations alone
claim: This contradicts Table 1 a few lines below, which lists prop:corner-generators among the direct users of the symmetric Lévy-Khintchine uniqueness clause (A3). Its clause (4) also reads the Student-t Thorin measure, which is conditional.
probe: Read the axiom output of the corner-generators declarations and reconcile the bullet with the table.

anchor: Student-t and stable families, the last under its hypothesis
claim: 'The last' of the list is the stable family, but Lemma subordinated-members proves the stable membership unconditionally. The conditional one is the Student-t membership (lem:student-subordinated, hypothesis grounded at rem:student-ggc). The trust-base summary puts the hypothesis on the wrong family.
probe: Check which membership carries the hypothesis against lem:subordinated-members and lem:student-subordinated, and attach it there.

anchor: Cited for orientation and used by no proof
claim: The caption says the closed form and Bessel tail of the Matérn kernel (A15, A16, prop:matern-density) are used by no proof. The proof of cor:matern-realization takes the exponential tail from prop:matern-density.
probe: List the proofs that cite prop:matern-density and either reroute the corollary's tail step (e.g. through prop:moments-tails) or list the corollary in the table.

anchor: it is the one this paper adds to the line paper's trust base
claim: Section 1.1, which this sentence cites ('as 1.1 said'), lists three facts added beyond the line paper (Bernstein, the moment criterion and tail floor, the density at the origin), plus A23 for the dimension filtration. The density at the origin is one of them, not 'the one'.
probe: Count the added facts in sec:machine-checked and match the sentence to that count.

anchor: the tail is super-exponential exactly when the profile has bounded support
claim: Proposition moments-tails(2) gives the order exp(-|x|log|x|/(tau t)) for bounded support, and for unbounded support only that the tail is heavier than every such rate. Heavier than every x log x rate does not exclude tails lighter than every exponential, so the 'only if' of 'super-exponential exactly when' is not stated by the proposition.
probe: Restate clause (2)'s dichotomy (the x log x order vs heavier than it) in the map, or check whether an unbounded but fast-decaying profile (e.g. Gaussian-decaying k) gives a super-exponential tail.

anchor: Student-t families of \S\ref{sec:corners} are one ray each
claim: The Matérn exponents gamma*log(1+omega^2) are positive multiples of one another, a ray. The Student-t exponents -log(2^{1-a}|omega|^a K_a(|omega|)/Gamma(a)) are not proportional across the shape a (prop:student-t(2)), so the family is a curve of rays, not one ray.
probe: Check proportionality of the Student-t exponents across a, and adjust the caption and the drawn Student-t ray.
